solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Armed soldiers annoy police, interrupted by separate odd bits of fire

indicators.note: separate says the two inserted letters are parted, the second moving on into the next word
the words for annoy and police each have a letter break into them

parts.note: to rile someone is to annoy them
cops is slang for police officers

indicators.note: the odd bits are the odd-numbered letters of the word fire, its first and third

explanation.surface: Irritated soldiers bother the police while scattered sparks of gunfire break out.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters of fire, F and R, are 'separate': F breaks into RILE and R into COPS, rather than going in as a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle corps is a body of soldiers armed with rifles, a regiment of riflemen.

clue.text: Way adult is apprehended by staff

indicators.note: being apprehended means being caught and held, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick
A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up is arrested by the staff of some institution.
explanation.definitionFit: A road is a route or way, as in 'the way to town'.

clue.text: Mood changes probing documents identifying ecological concern

indicators.note: something probing pokes into another thing, so these letters go inside

parts.note: files are documents kept on record

indicators.note: the word Mood changes its letter order

explanation.surface: Shifts of mood while investigating papers that point to an environmental worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'identifying' is a link: the wordplay identifies the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Food miles measure how far produce travels to the plate, an environmental worry about transport emissions.

clue.text: Each item in cupboard makes you decide against visiting restaurant

parts.note: ea is the standard abbreviation for each, as on price lists
a tin of food is a typical thing stored in a kitchen cupboard

explanation.surface: Every item stocked in the larder persuades you not to go out for dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat in is to have a meal at home rather than dine out at a restaurant.

clue.text: Fuel container, unusual, at bottom of ruined lido

indicators.note: in a down entry, being at the bottom of something places this piece after it
something ruined is wrecked, so the word lido is broken and rebuilt

parts.note: rum is old slang for odd or unusual

explanation.surface: An odd fuel tank sits at the bottom of a derelict open-air pool.
explanation.walkthrough: A lido is a public outdoor swimming pool. In a down light, 'at bottom of' puts the second piece below, so after, the first.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil drum is a large metal barrel used to hold fuel oil.

clue.text: Longing to fill a jug

indicators.note: filling a container means going inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: per means a, as in 'ten pounds a head'
an itch is a restless longing or desire

explanation.surface: Craving to top up a jug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' looks like a throwaway article but stands for PER, as in 'twice a day'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitcher is a large jug with a lip and handle for pouring.

clue.text: Display special methodology

parts.note: the how of something is its method or way of doing it

explanation.surface: Demonstrate a particular technique.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean an exhibition or presentation, or the act of putting something on view.

clue.text: Poet in reading for schoolchildren?

parts.note: being in means being at home
R stands for reading, one of the three Rs taught to schoolchildren

explanation.surface: A poet appearing on the school reading list.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs of schooling are reading, writing and arithmetic, hence R. The surface also nods to Homer being read in class.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer is the ancient Greek epic poet credited with the Iliad and Odyssey.

clue.text: Cynical concern about a weld coming loose

indicators.note: one piece placed about another goes around it

parts.note: worry and concern both mean anxiety

indicators.note: a weld coming loose falls apart, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doubter fretting that a welded joint is coming apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cynical' is a loose fit: world-weary people tend to be jaded and sceptical.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone world-weary is jaded and disillusioned, tired of life, which is close to cynical.

clue.text: Busy at the back pinching rings

indicators.note: pinching means gripping, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: aft is the nautical word for at the back of a ship
two letter Os look like two rings

explanation.surface: Someone occupied at the rear, stealing jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Afoot means under way or in progress, as with something going on or active.

clue.text: Molten metal core not an early development?

indicators.note: molten metal is melted and reshaped, so these letters are recast

explanation.surface: The fluid metal core of a planet, which formed later rather than early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Molten' melts and recasts METAL CORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A latecomer is someone or something arriving late, the opposite of an early arrival.

clue.text: Instrument of particular quality chopped up, gaining cheers

indicators.note: gaining means acquiring an addition, so the next piece is attached
in a down entry, up means the letters read from bottom to top
chopped means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: select means of choice or particular quality
ta is British informal for thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: A finely made instrument cut up while the audience cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped' cuts SELECT to SELEC, and 'up' turns that to CELES.
explanation.definitionFit: The celesta is a keyboard instrument whose hammers strike metal plates, giving a bell-like sound.

clue.text: One working to rule in demonstration about working

indicators.note: one piece placed about another surrounds it

parts.note: a march is a protest demonstration
on means working or operating, as with a switched-on machine

explanation.surface: A trade unionist on a work-to-rule protest marches in a demonstration about working conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working to rule' suggests industrial action, but here it means someone whose job is to reign.
explanation.definitionFit: A king or queen is a person whose role is to reign over a realm.

clue.text: According to text, you are in hat that's sensational

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
in text-message spelling 'you are' is shortened to UR

explanation.surface: A text message tells you that you are wearing an eye-catching hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid means shocking or graphically vivid, as in a lurid tabloid headline.

clue.text: Religious figure about to address God with quiet work on graffiti?

indicators.note: the first piece goes around the others

parts.note: a saint is a holy figure in religion
to pray is to speak to God
p is the musical notation for piano, meaning quiet

explanation.surface: A holy man prays quietly over his work on graffiti.
explanation.walkthrough: P for quiet comes from musical notation (piano). The question mark flags that the definition describes the answer by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Spray-painting is how most graffiti is applied, so it is work on graffiti.

clue.text: Traveller detailed building filth (in both instances)

indicators.note: de-tailed means the tail, the final letter, is cut off

parts.note: a pile is a large imposing building

indicators.note: this says the same tail-cutting applies to the second word as well

parts.note: grime is dirt or filth

explanation.surface: A traveller describes in detail a building's dirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' is read as de-tailed, losing the last letter; 'in both instances' applies it to PILE and GRIME alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilgrim is someone who makes a journey to a holy place, so a kind of traveller.

clue.text: List, being ramshackle?

definitions.meaning: a summary or itemised briefing, a quick overview of points
dilapidated or in poor condition, as a neglected house

explanation.surface: A catalogue of things that are falling apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A rundown is a summary list; run-down means shabby and dilapidated.

clue.text: One pound kept back in pay increase? That's ridiculous

indicators.note: the pieces are placed inside the word for a pay rise

parts.note: a rise is a British term for a pay increase
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: kept back means held in reverse, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: Only a single pound added in a pay rise? Absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: LB for pound comes from the Latin libra; a rise is British for a pay increase.
explanation.definitionFit: Risible means laughable, deserving of mockery, so absurd.

clue.text: Crowd absorbed by a lot of dancing in lightweight piece

indicators.note: being absorbed means being taken inside, so one piece goes into the other
a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: ballet is a form of theatrical dancing
the gate is the attendance or crowd at a sports match

explanation.surface: A crowd caught up in a big dance show, watching something trivial.
explanation.walkthrough: The gate is British for the crowd at a football match. 'a lot of' drops just the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagatelle is a short light piece of music, or a trifle.

clue.text: As for this, it can be disseminated in scare

indicators.note: disseminated means spread around, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A rumour that something can be spread as a panic.
explanation.walkthrough: As is the chemical symbol for the element; 'disseminated' rearranges IN SCARE.
explanation.definitionFit: The chemical symbol As stands for this poisonous element.

clue.text: I'd raised temperature in centre? This produces explosion

indicators.note: the pieces are placed inside the word for centre

parts.note: the core is the centre of something

indicators.note: raised in a down entry means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: the contraction I'd taken as its letters

explanation.surface: Turning up the heat in the core of a reactor triggers a blast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' works as a reversal because this is a down light, read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordite is a smokeless propellant explosive, used in shells and cartridges.

clue.text: Crow: small creature with tail?

parts.note: an animal with a tail can wag it, so whimsically it is a wagger

explanation.surface: A crow, a little bird with a tail feather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crow' looks like the bird but is the verb, to brag.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to boast, and to swagger is to strut boastfully.

clue.text: Mike, in breaking lock, shows key

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it

parts.note: a seal closes something up, like a lock
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Mike, breaking a lock, reveals a key.
explanation.walkthrough: M and IN break into SEAL: SE-MIN-AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Seminal means highly influential, crucial in later developments, so key.

clue.text: Hopes tomatoes will be used in bottling this sauce

indicators.note: something bottling holds contents inside, so the letters are concealed within these words

explanation.surface: A cook hopes the tomatoes will go into jars of this sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian sauce of basil, pine nuts, garlic and parmesan.

clue.text: Organisation — and in Bordeaux — involved in booze?

indicators.note: being involved in something means being inside it

parts.note: to sup is to drink, here taken as booze
et is French for and, the language of Bordeaux

explanation.surface: An outfit that goes along to Bordeaux, mixed up in wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-up is the arrangement or structure of an operation, an organisation.

clue.text: Odd item in tirade about men at sea

indicators.note: one piece goes around another

parts.note: a rant is an angry tirade

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A strange object turns up in a rant about sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd item' looks like part of the surface but is the definition: a leftover piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A remnant is a leftover bit, an odd piece remaining, like a fabric offcut.

clue.text: Address seemingly without a rent

indicators.note: without means lacking, so letters are taken out

parts.note: apparently means seemingly

explanation.surface: Someone's postal address, apparently with no rent to pay.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing ARENT from APPARENTLY leaves APP and LY.
explanation.definitionFit: To address a task is to apply oneself to it, giving it attention.

clue.text: Try taking up group therapy at the outset

indicators.note: in a down entry, taking up means lifting the word, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a set is a group

indicators.note: at the outset means only the very first letter of therapy is used

explanation.surface: Try joining group therapy from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking up' reverses SET to TES.
explanation.definitionFit: A test is a trial, an attempt to see how something works.

clue.text: Negligence, disregarding a team's initial purpose

indicators.note: disregarding means ignoring, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: inattention is carelessness or negligence

indicators.note: the initial of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A team's carelessness undermines its original aims.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing A and T (initial of team's) from INATTENTION leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An intention is an aim or plan, the purpose behind an action.

clue.text: Beat up on return to London college

indicators.note: on return means coming back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: LSE is the London School of Economics

explanation.surface: Beaten up on going back to a London college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on return' reverses UP to PU.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse is a regular rhythmic beat, as of the heart.

clue.text: Mistake that could make man mad?

definitions.text: Mistake that could make man mad?

parts.words: Mistake that could make man mad?
parts.note: a single wrong letter in printing could turn man into mad, so the clue describes such a slip

explanation.definitionFit: A typographical slip changes a letter, turning one printed word into another.

clue.text: Introduction of desk job saving first male from military action

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening letter
saving means except, so the letter is left out

parts.note: employment is a job

indicators.note: first here asks for the opening letter of the word male, its standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Starting a desk job keeps the first man away from combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving' is used in its sense 'except': only the first of the two Ms in EMPLOYMENT goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Deployment is the moving of troops into position for action.
